sponsor_or_proposer: Government of Togo (Ministry of Energy and Mining Resources) under the World Bank-backed PRIME-GAS regional program (Côte d'Ivoire-Togo-Benin); no commercial sponsor
current_state: Feasibility-study phase (2026): PRIME-GAS plans LNG reception and storage infrastructure at the Port of Lomé, a domestic gas network for future power plants (incl. a possible 500 MW gas-fired plant), and a pipeline from the port to the Adétikopé Industrial Platform. World Bank classified it high E&S risk and triggered a ~20-week strategic environmental and social assessment (corridor evaluation underway, May 2026). Regional context: 8 Dec 2025 CI-Benin-Togo pooled-LNG-imports declaration. Historical antecedent: 2018 Togo-Equatorial Guinea protocol on LNG supply/storage/regas at Lomé that never advanced.
missing_threshold_elements: No commercial sponsor/developer, no terminal configuration (FSRU vs onshore unspecified), no capacity, no tender, no FID timeline — government/World Bank studies only, below the add bar.
watch_for: SESA completion and corridor publication, terminal configuration choice (FSRU charter would be decisive), developer/tender selection, World Bank financing approval (project appraisal document would carry specifics).
